issues.legal_issue: Income derived from property during wrongful possession may be included in a mesne-profits assessment when the earlier decree does not clearly exclude it, while retained improvements may be taken into account in fixing the recoverable amount.
material_facts: The manager had converted a stable and an elephant stand into income-producing premises by adding walls and partitions, and those alterations were retained when possession was delivered to the owner.
The manager argued that observations in the earlier possession proceedings prevented a claim for income from those properties in the later mesne-profits inquiry.
The earlier judgment was not before the Court, and the High Court had considered the retained improvements when allowing only part of the estimated income.
issues.conclusion: The income claims were not shown to be barred by the earlier judgment, and the High Court's allowance for the retained improvements was fair and did not warrant interference.
issues.legal_principle: The Court could not determine that the earlier judgment barred the income claims without the judgment itself; in assessing mesne profits, it was proper to account for improvements that the former manager was not removing and that remained for the owner's benefit. No earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: mesne_profit_assessment and earlier_judgment_not_shown and income_producing_property and improvements_retained_for_owner

predicates.mesne_profit_assessment: The proceeding sought an assessment of profits from property held by another person.
predicates.earlier_judgment_not_shown: The judgment said to restrict the income claim was not before the court deciding the assessment.
predicates.income_producing_property: The property was used to produce or was capable of producing income.
predicates.improvements_retained_for_owner: The former possessor left improvements on the property for the owner's benefit.

issues.definition: When an income-producing property is assessed for mesne profits, the income may be considered despite an earlier judgment that is not shown, and retained improvements for the owner's benefit may be allowed for in the assessment.

issues.legal_issue: A court assessing mesne profits may estimate income from the evidence available when the person who controlled the relevant accounts does not produce them.
material_facts: The manager did not produce several of his accounts during the inquiry into mesne profits.
The courts assessed the income from the evidence that was produced, including evidence examined by a commissioner.
The Supreme Court found no basis to disturb the High Court's assessments for the disputed properties.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's assessments based on the evidence available were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Where relevant accounts were not produced, the court had to do its best to ascertain profits from the evidence before it. The Court identified no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this evidentiary ruling.

predicates.mesne_profit_assessment: The proceeding sought an assessment of profits from property held by another person.
predicates.relevant_accounts_not_produced: The person who controlled relevant accounts did not produce them in the assessment proceeding.
predicates.available_evidence_considered: The court assessed the income using the other evidence presented by the parties.

issues.definition: In a mesne-profits assessment, when relevant accounts are not produced, an income estimate based on the evidence that is available may be upheld.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may decline to entertain a statutory-amendment argument that was not raised in the court below or preserved in the appeal materials.
material_facts: The manager argued in the Supreme Court that an amendment restricting post-decree interest prevented interest being awarded on an aggregate that included interest.
The argument had not been made before the High Court and was not raised in the grounds seeking the appeal or in the statement of case.
The Supreme Court noted that the amendment's applicability and potential effect on substantive rights would require consideration, but declined to permit the new argument.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the amendment argument because it had not been raised earlier or properly preserved.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural principle that an appellate court may refuse to consider a point not raised below or preserved for appeal. It did not decide the amendment's applicability or whether it operated retrospectively.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter was a civil appeal.
predicates.amendment_argument_not_raised_below: The party did not present the statutory-amendment argument to the court below.
predicates.amendment_argument_not_preserved: The party did not include the argument in the appeal grounds or other appeal materials identified by the court.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, an appellate court may decline a statutory-amendment argument that the party neither raised below nor preserved in the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on mesne profits is calculated on the yearly profits as they accrue, with interest thereafter on the appropriate aggregate, and a reasonable trial-court rate should not be reduced without a sufficient basis.
material_facts: The manager remained in wrongful possession and appropriated income from property to which the owner was entitled.

The trial court awarded interest at six per cent, while the High Court reduced the rate before and after its decree, citing the manager's former trustee role, the mixing of properties held in different capacities, and the size of the decree.
The Supreme Court found no compelling equitable reason for the reduction and held that the yearly-profit method adopted by the High Court was correct.
The Supreme Court relied on the definition of mesne profits in Section 2(12) and the interest provision in Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.conclusion: The yearly-profit method was affirmed, but the High Court's reduced rates were set aside and the trial court's rate was restored for the calculation before and after the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(12) of the Code of Civil Procedure, interest is an integral part of mesne profits because a person wrongfully possessing property receives the benefit of the income. Section 34 permits the court to award reasonable interest. A former manager's status, the mixing of property held in distinct capacities, and a large decree did not justify reducing a reasonable trial-court rate in the circumstances. No earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: mesne_profit_proceeding and wrongful_possession and yearly_profits_accrued and trial_interest_rate_reasonable and no_compelling_basis_for_reduction

predicates.mesne_profit_proceeding: The proceeding concerned profits payable for property held by another person.
predicates.wrongful_possession: The person against whom profits were claimed wrongfully retained possession of the property.
predicates.yearly_profits_accrued: Income or profits arose from the property over successive periods.
predicates.trial_interest_rate_reasonable: The trial court's interest rate was not unreasonable in itself.
predicates.no_compelling_basis_for_reduction: The circumstances relied on for reducing interest did not establish a sufficient equitable reason for doing so.

issues.definition: When wrongful possession produces profits over time and the trial rate is reasonable, interest is calculated on the yearly profits as they accrue, and the rate should not be reduced without a sufficient basis.

issues.legal_issue: The value of improvements retained for the owner's benefit may be considered when fixing mesne profits if the former possessor could have removed those improvements before surrendering possession.
material_facts: The manager had made improvements to two properties, and it was common ground that he was not removing them.
The improvements had been made well before possession was surrendered, but the manager could have demolished or removed them under the law before surrendering the properties.
The High Court reduced the income otherwise assessed to account for the improvements left on the properties.
issues.conclusion: The High Court did not err in making an allowance for the retained improvements.
issues.legal_principle: A court fixing mesne profits may take account of improvements that the former possessor could have removed before surrendering possession but left for the owner's benefit. The Court relied on no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.mesne_profit_assessment: The proceeding sought an assessment of profits from property held by another person.
predicates.improvements_retained_for_owner: The former possessor left improvements on the property for the owner's benefit.
predicates.former_possessor_could_remove_improvemen: The former possessor could have removed or demolished the improvements before surrendering the property.

issues.definition: In a mesne-profits assessment, improvements left for the owner may be reflected in the amount assessed when the former possessor could have removed them before surrender.

issues.legal_issue: A court need not reopen the interpretation of a decree's collection-charge allowance when the parties jointly worked out the resulting amount on the same understanding.
material_facts: The manager disputed whether the High Court's judgment allowed a particular collection-charge deduction for house property.
After the judgment, the parties filed a joint memorandum calculating the mesne profits on the basis they both understood the judgment to require.
The decree was drawn up on the basis of that joint memorandum.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the collection-charge objection as groundless and did not reconsider the disputed interpretation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the parties' joint calculation, made on their shared understanding of the judgment, as a reason not to reopen the issue. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter was a civil appeal.
predicates.decree_amount_worked_out_by_joint_memo: The parties jointly submitted a memorandum calculating the amount due under the judgment.
predicates.parties_shared_interpretation: The parties used the same understanding of the judgment in preparing that calculation.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, when parties jointly calculate the decree amount using a shared interpretation of the judgment, the court need not reopen that interpretation.
